So... this was a big thing on [redacted], how if you posted something and people like it, it was well received. HOWEVER if anyone ever noticed that you were affiliated with it? Hate, calls of spam, and removal.

I get we don't want this place to turn into a spamfest, however we already have mechanics to prevent that, more so here since CCP and SCP regulate activity. If your stuff is downvoated, it'll fall to the bottom and get removed, along with your abilities to post more. There needs to be some balance but as a mid-level content creator I hate the double standard, and I bet a lot of others do to. People who are established? They can self-promote all they want, but people who aren't are hated for their efforts, even if the content in a vacuum is accepted.

I know there are probably a lot of us who make cool shit (or at least we think it is) and would like to share that, I just want the community to give people the opportunity organically, without having to hope someone else posts it.

Might seem ranty, might seem preachy, but I wanted to know what you thought?
What are your thoughts on OC submissions?
I think OC is great, providing it isn't just blatant self promotion.

Where's the line though? Submitting a gif or some screenshots, or posting a whole ad? I think the line is beyond a well-formatted post, especially one that isn't just "BUY MY SHIT", but others disagree. Where do you find the line to be?

Similar to you, if you're posting content that the community enjoys, then it should be fine.

However if your post is "I made this buy it/check it out" then I'd consider that spam.
OC as in "I made X, what do you think", instead of having to go through the "My friend/girlfriend/random person I don't know/anyone not me" made this charade.
I'm a big fan of people sharing original stuff.

I find it obnoxious when it's either blatant or some attempt at covering it up. That said, I think people should post whatever they feel like...particularly, if they think it will be enjoyed by others. I'm not going to go around downvoting someone just because they made something cool and want to make a living. Equally, I don't have a problem with sharing their websites. I'd prefer they stick around and not just post that material. But it all comes down to personal preference.
Can't wait to see you post more 'round these parts!

Pop on over to /v/cyclonenation to see the problem I'm having. Currently I have a banner image with 58px of white space below the image I actually want showing. I then position the image "left bottom" of the header and it shows correctly in full screen mode. However, when Voat is in a narrow window (fewer than 950px) the link bar at the top and the title bar (at the bottom of the header) change sizes, and it exposes white space above the image and covers up the bottom of the image.

Alternative configuration/same problem: I tried simply setting the banner image position to "0px 24px", but when the top link bar shrinks to 16px, the same problem arises.

Is there a way to set the height or position of the banner image to basically be glued to the bottom of the top link bar?

Edit - Here's what the header CSS is:

#header {
 background-image: url('http://i.imgur.com/QQQBNjZ.png');
 height: 159px !important;
 background-position: left bottom;
}

Edit 2 - PROBLEM SOLVED

I replaced my header CSS with the following, and it solved the issue (escape characters don't seem to work entirely with Voat's version of markdown, ignore the "\" ahead of the media tag):

\@media all and (max-width: 950px){
 #header {
 background-image: url('http://i.imgur.com/QQQBNjZ.png');
 background-position: 0px 17px;
 height: 159px !important;
 }
}

\@media all and (min-width: 951px){
 #header {
 background-image: url('http://i.imgur.com/QQQBNjZ.png');
 height: 159px !important;
 background-position: 0px 23px;
 }
}
